settings.heading: What does the carat weight on a bracelet mean?
settings.body:
On a tennis bracelet the carat figure is the total across every stone, not the size of any one of them. Two 5ct bracelets can look quite different: one of forty small diamonds, one of twenty-five larger ones. Compare the stone size and count as well as the total, and ask us if a listing leaves you unsure.

  • Natural or lab-grown diamonds in the same settings. Both are diamonds; lab-grown usually allows a heavier bracelet for the same spend.
  • Platinum, 18ct, 14ct or 9ct gold, hallmarked at a UK Assay Office where the law requires it.
  • Made to the length you need: measure your wrist and tell us when you order.

settings.title: What is a tennis bracelet?
settings.content: A tennis bracelet is a flexible line of diamonds of the same size and cut, each in its own setting, joined so the bracelet moves with the wrist. The name comes from the 1978 US Open, when Chris Evert stopped a match to find the diamond bracelet that had fallen from her wrist. Look for a box clasp with a safety catch.

settings.title: Should I choose natural or lab-grown diamonds for a bracelet?
settings.content: Both are diamonds, with the same hardness and sparkle; the difference is origin and price. Because a bracelet carries many stones, lab-grown often means a heavier total weight or a higher grade for the same spend. Natural stones carry rarity and a documented origin. We set both and will not push you towards either.

settings.title: Which metal is best for a bracelet worn every day?
settings.content: Platinum is the most durable and stays white without plating. 18ct gold has the richest colour; 9ct gold is harder-wearing and paler. White gold is rhodium plated and needs replating every few years to keep its bright finish. Pieces are hallmarked at a UK Assay Office where the law requires it, so the metal and fineness are stamped on them.

settings.title: How do I find the right bracelet length?
settings.content: Measure snugly around the wrist bone and add 1.5 to 2 cm. Made-to-order bracelets are made to the length you need, so tell us your measurement when you order; ready-made bracelets are listed with their length. A bracelet should move freely but never slide over the hand. Bangles need their inside diameter checked instead.

settings.title: Can I wear a diamond bracelet every day?
settings.content: Yes, if it is well made and you treat it as fine jewellery. Take it off for exercise, the gym and manual work, where it can catch or take a knock. Check the clasp closes firmly, and bring it in for its free inspection if anything feels loose.

settings.title: Can a bracelet be shortened or lengthened later?
settings.content: Shortening a tennis bracelet means removing links, which we can do. Lengthening means adding links with matching diamonds and metal, which is possible but harder than ordering the right length at the start. Bangles and cuffs are made to size and cannot be altered.

settings.title: Can a bracelet be engraved?
settings.content: Some of our bracelets can be engraved, and the listing says when engraving is available. We send you a proof before anything is engraved, and hand engraving adds about a week.

settings.title: How long does a bracelet take?
settings.content: We confirm the delivery time for your bracelet before you order: made-to-order bracelets need making time, while ready-made bracelets do not. If you have a date to hit, tell us before you order and we will say honestly whether we can make it.

settings.title: Can I return a bracelet?
settings.content: Ready-made bracelets can be returned within 14 days of delivery, unworn and in their original packaging. Made-to-order and bespoke bracelets are made for you, so we do not offer change-of-mind returns on them, which is why we talk each order through first. If a bracelet arrives faulty or not as ordered, you can reject it for a full refund within 30 days; after that we repair or replace it under our lifetime warranty.
